lesson_title: Formulas Are Machines: Run Them Both Ways
hook_text: One wrong button and your bakkie hire costs R101 270. Here's the button.
clip_script: Now compute — and here stands the great trap of forward substitution: the order of operations. Multiplication before addition, always. The wrong road adds first: 380 plus 9,50 gives 389,50, times 260 gives a monstrous R101 270 — a bakkie-hire bill that buys the bakkie. The right road multiplies first. So: 9,50 times 260 gives 2 470. Then add the fixed charge: 380 plus 2 470 equals 2 850. The 260 kilometre trip costs R2 850. Sense-check it against the story: the trip charge should dwarf the entrance fee on a long drive. Reasonable.
visual_style: Split-screen calculator race: the wrong keystroke order exploding into a giant red R101 270, the correct order landing calmly on R2 850 with a green tick.
pacing: Fast disaster reveal, slower correct walkthrough, snappy sense-check close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to run the formula backwards too.
